narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
intent: To explain the global prevalence of lactose intolerance and the biological mechanism behind it.

units.meaning: Lactose intolerance affects 65% of the global population.
accepted_routes: Worldwide, about 65% of the population is lactose intolerant.
Lactose intolerance has a global prevalence of 65%.
Roughly two-thirds of people worldwide are lactose intolerant.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The chart must show the Lactose Intolerant category with a label, value, or mark at 65% (or the equivalent 0.65 share of the whole).
units.temporal_anchor: The clause stating the worldwide prevalence of lactose intolerance.
units.reviewer_question: Is the 65% global prevalence of lactose intolerance obligatory in the video?

units.meaning: Lactose tolerance affects 35% of the global population.
accepted_routes: About 35% of the world population is lactose tolerant.
A little over a third are lactose tolerant.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The chart must show the Lactose-Tolerant category with a label, value, or mark at 35% (or the equivalent 0.35 share of the whole).
units.temporal_anchor: Any clause presenting the lactose-tolerant or complementary share, if included.
units.reviewer_question: Is showing the 35% lactose-tolerant share obligatory or optional?

units.meaning: Lactose intolerance is nearly twice as common as lactose tolerance.
units.computation: 65 / 35 = 1.857..., so intolerance is about 1.9 times tolerance.
accepted_routes: Lactose intolerance is almost twice as prevalent as lactose tolerance.
65% vs 35%: intolerance is roughly 1.9 times as common.
The intolerant group is about 1.86 times the tolerant group.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The chart must allow comparing the two category sizes, e.g., bars with relative lengths or labels showing 65% and 35%.
units.temporal_anchor: The clause comparing the two groups, if present.
units.reviewer_question: Is the comparative ratio/ordering between the two groups obligatory or optional?

units.meaning: Lactose intolerance is the majority condition (more than half of the population), while lactose tolerance is the minority.
units.computation: 65 > (65+35)/2 = 50, and 35 < 50, so intolerant is the majority and tolerant is the minority.
accepted_routes: More than half the world is lactose intolerant.
Lactose intolerance is the majority condition.
Lactose tolerance is the minority share (35%).
units.visual_evidence_rule: The chart must make the 65% share visibly exceed half of the total, or the narration must state majority/minority.
units.temporal_anchor: The clause framing the 65% as the larger/majority group.
units.reviewer_question: Is the majority/minority framing required or optional?

units.meaning: The two categories together account for 100% of the population (65% + 35%), i.e., they are complementary shares of the whole.
accepted_routes: Lactose intolerance and lactose tolerance together make up the whole population.
The two shares are complementary: 65% intolerant and 35% tolerant.
Together the two categories sum to 100%.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The chart must show both categories as parts of one whole, or otherwise make their complementary relationship explicit.
units.temporal_anchor: The clause that presents both shares together, if included.
units.reviewer_question: Is the complementary 100% composition required or optional?

unsupported_to_avoid: The 150 millilitres per day limit mentioned in the narration (not in table).
The absence of the enzyme after infancy and other biological mechanism details (causal claims not in table).
Any claim that lactose intolerance causes specific symptoms or digestive limits beyond the table.
Any percentage, count, or value not derivable from the table cells (e.g., 150 ml, enzyme levels).
Extrapolation to time trends or other populations not represented.
notes: The data table supports only the 65% intolerant and 35% tolerant prevalence split; mechanism details and 150 ml limit are outside the table. Required flag is set only for the core 65% prevalence, with comparison, complement, and majority framing offered as optional valid units.
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
